title: No flour, no Torah (Avot 3:17)
hookLine: Elazar ben Azariah: without bread there's no Torah, without Torah no bread
tomorrow: a tree with lots of branches: why does the wind win?

cards: Nobody does their best thinking on a skipped lunch; a vending machine the night before a final knows it. Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah said it as a pair of mirrors: im ein kemach ein Torah, im ein Torah ein kemach.
If there's no flour, there's no Torah. If there's no Torah, there's no flour.

teach.b: Underneath is an old question: which comes first, the body or the soul? Elazar's answer: neither one alone. The first half is plain.
People who are hungry can't learn, so feeding them is holy work, not a break from it. The second half turns around. Flour with no Torah, a living with nothing wise to guide it, won't hold up either.
He strings more pairs on the same line: no wisdom without awe, no awe without wisdom; no knowledge without understanding, and back again.

A Christian neighbor asks the same question in the Letter of James, in the King James words: "If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food, And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit?"
Both refuse to bless a hungry person and walk away.
One honest difference: James is asking what faith is worth without deeds. Elazar's mirror also faces the other way, and asks what bread is worth without learning.

how: Jews say a blessing before eating bread, and Jewish communities have long kept funds and kitchens for the hungry; Avot 3:17 is studied as a reason both belong with learning.

o: a fast that ends with study instead of food
without bread there's no learning, and back again
a rule against baking bread on holy days

games.q: the two mirrors — tap the pairs.

s: Elazar ben Azariah says learning matters and bread doesn't
no flour, no Torah: the learning needs bread.
the Letter of James asks what good it is to send a hungry person off with words
Elazar's line only works in one direction
no Torah, no flour, too: the mirror faces both ways.

games.q: a friend is cramming for finals on chips and no sleep and won't stop for dinner. by Elazar's line, what do you say?
o: eat first. no flour, no Torah: the studying needs the bread.
keep going; real learning means ignoring the body.
skip the exam; bread matters more than learning.
games.why: if there's no flour, there's no Torah, and the mirror runs both ways: the bread serves the learning too.

practice: If there's something to eat or drink nearby, take one slow bite or sip and taste it all the way through. If not, bring to mind the last meal someone made or bought for you, and the hands behind it.
If you say a blessing before food, this is a good place for it.

wordCard.voice: No flour. Kemach, flour: the plainest need on Elazar's list, and the one learning can't skip.

orig.note: Hebrew: flour, meal; Elazar ben Azariah's word for the basic needs of life.

carryVoice: No flour, no Torah, and the mirror runs both ways, from the kitchen to the study and back. Shalom.
